extracted.intended_audience: grant reviewers, translational researchers, and preclinical investigators in transplantation/cell therapy
extracted.subtask_description: A Phase I preclinical research plan testing whether ex vivo–expanded myeloid progenitor cells (MPc/MP) can induce antigen-specific tolerance to solid organ grafts in mouse models (skin and trachea/lung). Includes experimental design, endpoints, milestone criteria, animal use, and product lot-release criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary outcome for Aim 1 — tracheal graft occlusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary outcome will be airway occlusion assessed on H&E stained slides; milestone: demonstrate that allogeneic tracheas have significantly reduced luminal occlusion (<50% occlusion by surface area on all cross sections of H&E stained slides) beyond 30 days post transplant in mice given MP matching the trachea graft prior to or simultaneous with transplant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control groups on the same mice include (i) tracheas that do not match MP (or HSC or host) that should be occluded, and (ii) tracheas matched to HSC or host that should not occlude. Secondary sign: loss of epithelium visible on H&E sections scored as percent circumference without epithelium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary outcome for Aim 2 — skin/trachea graft acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary outcome is skin (or trachea) graft acceptance or rejection based on gross morphology, confirmed by histology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skin grafts are followed (photography) and independently scored for acceptance/rejection. Trachea acceptance assessed as epithelial maintenance/absence of occlusion. Use paired analyses where applicable (three grafts per mouse for trachea).

rubrics_metrics.name: Milestone/acceptance thresholds and re-test decision rules (Aim 2 dose/matching)
rubrics_metrics.description: Milestone: determine ability of standard doses of MP (10^6 cells obtained after expansion) to protect grafts that are fully matched, MHC-major matched, or haploidentical to the MP; group size 15 mice per group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If failure is observed (ten or more rejected grafts out of 15) the group will be repeated using trachea grafts (if Aim 1 successful) and an increased dose (5x10^6) of expanded MP; group size will remain fifteen for sufficient power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lot release testing for cryopreserved MPc
rubrics_metrics.description: All cryopreserved MPc will undergo lot release testing that includes viability, composition, function, endotoxin levels, and bioburden to ensure a product with consistent purity and potency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lot release is performed to ensure consistent clinical-grade product; tests include measures of cell viability, cellular composition (phenotype), functional assays, and standard sterility/endotoxin/bioburden controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental controls and expected control outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Include internal controls on the same mouse (MP-matched graft, HSC/host-matched graft, and unmatched graft). Expected outcomes: MP-matched and HSC/host-matched grafts should not occlude/reject; unmatched grafts should be occluded/rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using multiple grafts per mouse (randomized placement) provides within-animal controls to strengthen comparisons and reduce variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size and statistical power
rubrics_metrics.description: With 15 mice in each group at alpha = 0.05 there is at least 80% power to detect a difference in percentage of animals with the primary outcome of 0.6, assuming grafts have a correlation of 0.2 or less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group sizes of 15 were chosen for power; the protocol specifies paired analyses where appropriate and reiterates repeated experiments for validation of significant findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods and data-analysis rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary analyses: paired t-test for graft comparisons; survival analyses via Kaplan-Meier curves with Wilcoxon logrank test; use of parametric transformations (e.g., log) when necessary and nonparametric tests (Wilcoxon rank-sum) when assumptions are not met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Software: SPSS, Cytel StatXact, LogXact, SAS v9.01. Multiple imputations for missing items will be explored if data are missing at random; actual P-values will be reported and significant experiments repeated for validation. The two-step approach is noted because assays typically give clear acceptance/rejection outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Censoring and handling of early mortality/missing data
rubrics_metrics.description: Mice that die before analysis due to hematopoietic failure (<30 days post reconstitution) or infection (death <10 days post reconstitution) will be censored, as experiments are not designed to study HCT-associated morbidity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Causes of missing data will be examined. All possible data will be included in the analysis using appropriate methods; multiple imputation may be used if missing at random.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assay/flow cytometry endpoints and lineage/origin determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondary variables include number, origin, and types of cells present in reconstituted mice at various times, expressed as absolute cell numbers or percent; hematopoietic origin will be identified using 6-color flow cytometry with MHC class I or congenic markers (CD45).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flow cytometry will focus on detection of lymphocytes in graft and systemically; include mixed lymphocyte reactions (CellTrace Far Red labeled lymphocytes) to test activation/proliferation by irradiated host-, donor- or third-party lymphocytes as an in vitro assay of tolerance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomization and graft placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Order and actual position (front or back, left/right) of trachea/skin grafts will vary randomly; placement of multiple grafts (e.g., MP-matched, HSC-matched, unmatched) on the same mouse is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Random assignment of graft position reduces positional biases; placement of multiple differentially matched grafts per animal provides paired comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model/operational definitions for MP vs MPc and dosing regimens
rubrics_metrics.description: MP refers to purified myeloid progenitors; MPc refers to ex vivo–expanded and cryopreserved MP. Typical cell doses used: 10^5 FACS-purified MP or 10^6 MPc expanded from HSC for skin graft experiments; experimental adjustments (e.g., increase to 5x10^6) are pre-specified if tolerance is not achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons between directly sorted MP and expanded/cryopreserved MPc are part of evaluation; equivalence/noninferiority is assessed via graft survival metrics (example: 90% vs 81% skin graft survival, p=0.58 in prior data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of established, reproducible models and contingency plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary use of heterotopic tracheal transplant and established skin graft models (stringent). If questions cannot be answered, more complex orthotopic models (trachea or lung transplant) will be considered in Phase II or subsequent experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contingency options include increasing MP dose, changing culture conditions, or using freshly purified MP if culture-derived MPc fail; alternate transplant models (ear-heart) may be used to probe tolerance in less easily rejected models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animal care, ethics, and procedural standards
rubrics_metrics.description: All animal work is IACUC approved and will conform to institutional and PHS policies; described husbandry (strains, ages), euthanasia methods (CO2 asphyxiation followed by cervical dislocation), anesthesia and analgesia regimens (xylazine/ketamine for surgery, buprenorphine 0.05 mg/kg s.c. twice daily ×3 or more as needed), monitoring, and veterinary oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocols include justification for species/strain and numbers, veterinary care descriptions, peri-irradiation antibiotic use, anesthetic monitoring and recovery procedures, sterile surgical technique, and humane endpoints (monitor for distress and euthanize when moribund). These are required standards for ethical conduct and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural specifications for experimental reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed procedures provided for irradiation (e.g., 2x4.25 Gy, 4 hours apart or total 8-10 Gy depending on strain; RadSource 2000 irradiator settings), specific HSC/MP phenotypes and cell numbers for injection (e.g., CD117+, CD90.1lo, Lin-, Sca-1+ 4,000 cells for CD90.1 strains; 10^4 cells for CD90.2 strains), culture conditions (8-10 day expansion in Xvivo15 with SCF, Flt3L, Tpo), graft harvest and implantation techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit procedural details are required to reproduce experiments and to interpret whether milestones are met; these are treated as technical quality standards.
